newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon identifies parts from missing A-10 plane.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon identifies parts from missing A-10 plane.

text.p: Two small pieces of metal recovered from a snowy peak in the Rocky Mountains have been identified as parts of the wreckage of an A-10 warplane loaded with bombs that disappeared three weeks ago, a senior Air Force official said on Wednesday.
"They have identified the parts as part of Capt. Button's airplane," the official said. "They checked the serial numbers of the parts and they are from Capt. Button's aircraft."
The A-10 Thunderbolt piloted by Capt. Craig Button disappeared during a routine training mission on April 2.

The military was unable to locate the plane until Sunday, when wreckage was spotted by an Army National Guard helicopter crew near a steep cliff on New York Mountain near the Vail, Colorado, ski resort.

On Wednesday, a crewman from an MH-53 heavy lift helicopter was lowered to the side of the mountain. The largest piece of wreckage visible through snow was too big to lift, Air Force Major General Nels Running said in Denver.

The crewman then saw two small pieces nearby and brought them back for inspection. Both bore "manufacturer's nomenclature" and other markings that determined the wreckage was in fact the missing A-10.

The official said the Air Force would attempt to move more personnel to the area on Thursday in an attempt to locate Button, 32, who inexplicably left the three-plane formation in which he was flying and veered northeast into Colorado, some 850 miles (1,350 km) away.
The A-10 Thunderbolt attack bomber was thought to have slammed into the side of the 12,500-foot (3,800-metre) high New York Mountain in the remote Sawatch range southeast of Vail.
